heroLead: Fort Duchesne is the administrative seat of the Ute Indian Tribe and the Uintah and Ouray Reservation, and mineral ownership in this area requires a careful first step before anything else.
intro: Fort Duchesne sits within the boundaries of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation in Uintah County, home to the Ute Indian Tribe's government offices and a mix of tribal trust, allotted, and privately held fee mineral interests layered across the same sections. This is one of the more distinctive ownership patterns in the entire Uinta Basin, and it is important to be clear about which kind of interest you hold before discussing a sale.

We buy privately held fee mineral and royalty interests near Fort Duchesne. Tribal trust minerals and individual Indian allotment interests follow a separate transfer process through the Bureau of Indian Affairs that we do not handle directly, and we will tell you plainly if that applies to your situation rather than pretending otherwise.

sections.heading: Trust, allotted, and fee minerals — knowing which one you have
paragraphs: Original allotments made to individual tribal members under federal law created a pattern of ownership that, over generations of inheritance, has fractionated into interests held by many descendants, some of which remain in federal trust status and some of which passed out of trust into fee status through historical land transactions. If your family's interest near Fort Duchesne is fee simple — meaning it was conveyed out of trust status at some point and is now held like any other private mineral interest — we can typically make a direct purchase offer. If it remains in trust status, the BIA governs any transfer, and that is a different process than what we handle.

sections.heading: Confirming status before anything else
paragraphs: Because getting this distinction right matters, we start every inquiry near Fort Duchesne by confirming ownership status through the county recorder and, where relevant, checking whether BIA records show trust involvement. This is not a formality we skip to move faster — it is the first real step, and we would rather spend the time upfront than make an offer on something we cannot actually close.

faqs.question: How do I know if my mineral interest near Fort Duchesne is in trust status or fee status?
faqs.answer: We can help you check, starting with your deed or any BIA correspondence you have. If it is unclear, we will confirm before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Do you buy tribal trust or allotment interests?
faqs.answer: No, those transfer through a separate Bureau of Indian Affairs process. We only purchase privately held fee mineral interests.

faqs.question: My family's interest passed out of trust status generations ago. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It can — once minerals are held in fee status, they generally transfer like any other private interest, and we can typically make a direct offer once that status is confirmed.
